title: Cohomology comparison of coefficient Frobenius pairs with native Weil sheaves
statement: Fix a finite field datum D and coefficient setting P [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with prime ell different from the characteristic, and let a_0:X_0 -> Spec D.k0 be separated of finite type. Use the native derived Weil category and its homology sheaves [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let c_0 compactify a_0 and S be a coefficient-normalized exceptional adjunction system [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let Q be the common-stage geometric Frobenius pullback and Pairs its category of objects with an invertible structure QK -> K [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Define E_S as G_S(1) with structure the inverse-exchange right mate followed by G_S(theta_0); define T_d=H_d(1) with the actual root-line, tensor-unit and even-shift structure canonicalSourceTheta [def-pur-canonical-purity-source-transports, lem-pur-constant-purity-frobenius-square]. There exist functors C_n:Pairs -> WeilSheaf(D.k0,ell,X0), for every integer n, such that: (i) for every native right adjoint J of Ra_0! with its adjunction and every n, H^n(J(constant_point[0])) is isomorphic to C_n(E_S); (ii) for every natural d, C_(-2d)(T_d) is isomorphic to the native Tate sheaf(d) tensor the native constant sheaf [def-weil-constant-weil-structure, def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. No smoothness is assumed and no isomorphism E_S ~= T_d is asserted.

proof.text: Use the normalized exact common-stage realization, the section-module equivalence and equivariant algebraic-closure transport. Their Frobenius comparisons turn a coefficient Frobenius pair into a Frobenius pair in the ordinary derived category. Apply degree n cohomology and the exact-pullback cohomology comparison. The cohomology is bounded constructible, so the resulting pair is a native Weil sheaf. On arrows use cohomology of the same realization; the comparison naturality proves the intertwining condition and the functor laws. This constructs C_n for every integer n, without a derived fixed-pair equivalence.

proof.text: At any native exceptional adjunction J, use the counit-normalized exceptional-forgetting comparison at the constant object on the arithmetic point, and its scalar-unit normalization. Transport the native counit equivariance through the normalized compact-support comparison, then transpose through the ordinary adjunction. Uniqueness under its Hom equivalence identifies the action with the inverse-exchange right mate followed by G(theta_0), as computed by the scalar Frobenius counit theorem. Exact cohomology of this comparison is the first family of endpoint isomorphisms.

proof.text: For the canonical purity-source pair H_d(1), the normalized pullback-unit comparison identifies the ordinary unit factor. Tensor and root-line realization identifies the d-th Tate line, with its cyclotomic Frobenius, with the native Tate sheaf. Shift compatibility moves the even shift 2d to cohomological degree -2d; in that degree the unshifted sheaf remains. The tensor-unit convention gives precisely the Tate sheaf tensor the native constant. The maps used here are the root, unit, tensor and shift maps in canonicalSourceTheta, so the isomorphism respects Frobenius. This proves the second endpoint family. There is no use of smoothness or purity and no comparison between the exceptional and Tate endpoints in this lemma. For d=0 these are the unit comparisons; on the empty scheme all objects are zero.

lean.statement:
theorem coefficient_cohomology_comparison :
    ∃ C : ℤ → (Pairs P X₀ ⥤ WeilSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left),
      (∀ (J : WeilComplex P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l (Spec (.of P.field.k₀)) ⥤
          WeilComplex P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left)
        (adj : WeilComplex.derivedLowerShriek P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.hom ⊣ J)
        (n : ℤ),
        Nonempty ((WeilComplex.homologySheaf n).obj
            (J.obj (WeilSheaf.toComplex.obj
              (WeilSheaf.adicConstant P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l
                (Spec (.of P.field.k₀))))) ≅
          (C n).obj (exceptionalConstant P X₀ c₀ S))) ∧
      (∀ d : ℕ, Nonempty ((C (-2 * (d : ℤ))).obj (twistedConstant P X₀ d) ≅
        (WeilSheaf.tateTwistSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left d).tensorObj
          (WeilSheaf.adicConstant P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left)
          (WeilSheaf.isLisse_tateTwistSheaf P.field.k₀ P.coefficients.l X₀.left d)))
